source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 296: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 296): treat the initialization hang as an unproven symptom; do not infer a platform-specific cause. Use an authorized disposable allocation, redacted logs, a finite watchdog, and automatic cleanup. Keep launcher, image, placement, backend, world size, versions, and production settings fixed; label every fact measured, estimated, or unknown.

Hypotheses and falsification: the primary hypothesis is a rank-membership/rendezvous mismatch or collective-order divergence leaving a rank waiting. Competing hypotheses are incorrect GPU visibility or mapping, stale/unreachable rendezvous state, wrong interface/route/MTU/firewall, topology or peer-access faults, container/shared-memory limits, and CPU/RAM/file-descriptor exhaustion. The primary hypothesis is falsified only if every rank reports the same fresh attempt ID and world size, unique global/local rank, host, rendezvous endpoint, visible device UUID, selected interface, and identical collective sequence, and a checksum-verified minimal all-reduce completes on every rank within a stated timeout.

Measurements: capture per-rank launch/process-group arguments with credentials redacted; rendezvous reachability and timestamps; rank arrival/collective entry and exit times; backend logs; device UUIDs and visibility; interface, route, MTU, firewall, topology, peer-access, container IPC/shared-memory, ulimits, CPU/RAM, and clock data. First reproduce with a minimal all-reduce, then run repeated matched trials at single-node, reduced-world, and full-world sizes while changing one factor at a time; pin a finite timeout and record correctness, latency distribution, timeout/rank failure, transport choice, and cleanup results. A rank that differs in membership, order, or endpoint supports the primary hypothesis; a clean reduced-world run but full-world failure points to scale, placement, or fabric, not proof of one cause.

Confounders include scheduler placement, transient fabric faults, clock skew, stale stores, warm-up, library changes, and resource pressure. On timeout, preserve redacted evidence, terminate only the disposable trial, remove temporary rendezvous state, and revert any canary configuration. Require the raw per-rank records and repeated trial matrix before concluding; do not expose secrets or claim root cause without evidence.
risks: rank/order symptoms can be confounded by transient transport or scheduler faults
debug records may expose endpoint or topology metadata
a hung trial may orphan processes if watchdog cleanup fails
evidence_required: per-rank rendezvous, membership, and collective timestamps
repeated matched all-reduce results for single-node, reduced-world, and full-world conditions
version, topology, interface, resource, timeout, and cleanup records

source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 2: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 2): compare the same model revision, tokenizer, serving engine, hardware, precision constraints, prompt set, batching policy, concurrency, software build, and power/thermal policy. Quantization is weight-only; document bit width, group size, scales/zero-points, calibration data, outlier handling, kernel support, and any changed activation or KV-cache precision. Use a disposable, authorized benchmark and redact inputs that contain sensitive data; label measured values, estimates, and unknowns.

Falsifiable hypothesis: the candidate quantized model lowers cost per successful token while keeping quality and service-level objectives within predeclared tolerances. It is falsified if paired quality tests exceed the allowed regression, any safety/functional failure appears, or cost per successful output does not improve after accounting for calibration, memory, throughput, and operational overhead. Competing explanations include kernel incompatibility, dequantization overhead, calibration-set mismatch, memory-bandwidth saturation, batching differences, thermal throttling, and changed failure/retry behavior.

Controlled experiment: freeze prompts, ordering, seeds where meaningful, max input/output lengths, stop conditions, sampling policy, request mix, concurrency levels, batch limits, replicas, and power policy. Warm both systems identically, randomize A/B order, repeat independent runs, and use paired bootstrap confidence intervals or another prespecified method. Measure task quality and exact failure categories; peak GPU/CPU memory; TTFT and TPOT in milliseconds per request/token; tokens/s, requests/s, queueing, p50/p95/p99 latency, error/timeout/OOM rates, utilization, energy if available, and dollars per successful input/output token. Sweep realistic concurrency and report kernel/version/hardware support and calibration-set provenance. Do not average away tail failures; publish sample counts and exclusions.

Analyze quality and service metrics jointly, with confidence intervals and predefined equivalence/non-inferiority and cost thresholds. Investigate outlier prompts and long contexts separately. Confounders include prompt leakage, cache state, kernel fallback, NUMA placement, autoscaling, background load, thermal drift, and measurement overhead. If thresholds fail, retain the baseline, disable the candidate, keep only redacted reproducibility artifacts, and revert configuration; deployment requires review of evidence, safety cases, and rollback readiness.
risks: quality regression may be hidden by an unrepresentative calibration or prompt set
unsupported kernels may silently fall back and distort cost or latency
benchmark inputs and logs may contain sensitive data
evidence_required: paired quality and failure results with confidence intervals
memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, tail latency, and cost measurements
quantization configuration, calibration provenance, kernel/build, hardware, and rollback records
